title: Olmesartan in hypertension: RETIRED -- the titled drug is the comparator in all three trials and the intervention in none
question: Does olmesartan, as the intervention, improve blood pressure against a comparator? THIS TOPIC CANNOT ASK THAT QUESTION: no trial on this page tests olmesartan as the intervention.
topic_state: RETIRED -- no poolable result is possible for the question the title asks
completeness_statement: Three registrations were read in full from ClinicalTrials.gov. Identity was established before any number, and no number was extracted, because the intervention limb fails before an effect is relevant.
verification_basis: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.armGroups[].type and interventionNames[], read per trial on 2026-08-18. The arm TYPE is what distinguishes an intervention from a comparator; the interventions[] list alone cannot, because ClinicalTrials.gov lists comparators there too.

trials.label: Efficacy and Safety of Azilsartan Medoxomil Plus Chlorthalidone in Participants With Moderate to Severe Hypertension
Efficacy and Safety of Azilsartan Medoxomil and Chlorthalidone Compared to Olmesartan Medoxomil and Hydrochlorothiazide
Efficacy and Safety of LCZ696 in Comparison to Olmesartan in Japanese Patients With Essential Hypertension

outcomes.name: Change in blood pressure
outcomes.definition: Each of the three registrations declares a blood-pressure primary, so the OUTCOME limb passes. That is why an outcome-only screen passed this page and why it is retired on a different limb.

bp_change.poolable_reason: OLMESARTAN IS THE COMPARATOR IN ALL THREE TRIALS AND THE INTERVENTION IN NONE OF THEM. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: NCT00846365 and NCT01033071 test AZILSARTAN medoxomil plus chlorthalidone, and NCT01599104 tests LCZ696 (sacubitril/valsartan). In every one, olmesartan sits in the ACTIVE_COMPARATOR arm. THE TOPIC CONTAINS NO TRIAL IN WHICH ITS OWN TITLED DRUG IS THE INTERVENTION. This is what a drug-name search over trial records produces when it matches a name anywhere in the record rather than resolving it to an arm. It is not a topic with a defect; there is no honest version of the page, because no poolable result is possible for the question the title asks. AUTHORITY: Cochrane Handbook 6.5 (2024) section 10.10.3 -- 'Meta-analysis should only be considered when a group of studies is sufficiently homogeneous in terms of participants, interventions and outcomes to provide a meaningful summary' -- and MECIR Box 10.10.a C62, 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar'. The interventions here are azilsartan, azilsartan and LCZ696. NOTHING IS LOST BY RETIRING IT: the two azilsartan trials are the coherent core of the AZILSARTAN topic, and are recorded there.

bp_change.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that the three trials are poor -- all three are registered, randomised and report their primary. NOT that azilsartan or LCZ696 are ineffective; this page never asked about them. NOT that no olmesartan trial exists -- only that none is on this page.

risk_of_bias_verdict: Not assessed. A risk-of-bias assessment grades the trials that contribute to a result, and this page contributes none. Stated rather than left blank.
